resources.string: Two teams, one ball. Knock the ball into the goal at the far end to score. Your own goal is the one nearest you.
Pull back from one of your figures, like a slingshot, and let go. The figure shoots the way you pulled, harder the longer the pull.
Flick your figures into the ball. A figure can be flicked again once it stops. Your keeper springs back to the goal by itself.
Everyone plays at the same time. First to the goal target wins, or the most goals when the clock runs out. Level? Sudden death.
Want to take your time? Turn on Turn-based assist: the teams take turns and the table settles between flicks. Hint shows a good flick.
Flicking small figures across a cloth pitch goes back to Subbuteo, a table game first sold in England in 1947.
Your player runs to the ball by itself. You choose the shot and its moment with one swipe.
A ring closes around the spot where the ball will be hit. Swipe toward the net just as it closes: a perfectly timed swipe makes a perfect shot.
Swipe left or right of straight for the angle. Swipe faster for a harder, deeper shot, but a deep shot can land out.
To serve, the ball is tossed for you. Swipe at the top and land it in the opposite service box. Two faults lose the point.
Score like real tennis (0, 15, 30, 40) or race to a set number of points. Relaxed timing makes the ball wait for your swing.
The scores 15, 30 and 40 come from medieval France, and the word tennis probably comes from the French tenez, meaning take it.
